subject: URGENT: production p99 spikes + 429 retry cascade impacting Brightlane
messages:
From: Cicero Huang <cicero.huang@brightlane.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightlane.com; ceo@brightlane.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: PROD: p99 spike + 429s since 06:00PT — urgent

Tessa — we started seeing sustained p95/p99 latency spikes on the hosted API at ~06:00 PT and a cascading set of 429s across our fleet. User-facing timeouts are happening (~10% of requests for a subset of routes) and our client-side retry logic appears to be amplifying the tail (multiple rapid retries per request).

Attached is a short log extract and a p95/p99 chart from our telemetry team (p95 up 4x, p99 up 8x). We need an urgent sync to understand whether this is a Redwood-side rate-limiter behavior, a routing/backpressure issue, or a model runtime degradation.

Impact: checkout flows and chat widgets are timing out; revenue-impacting for customers in US-East. Please escalate and advise next steps.

Thanks,
Cicero
Cicero Huang
Platform Engineering Lead | Brightlane

Attachments: support-log-20270318.txt (log excerpt), p95-p99-trends-20270318.png (chart)

Subject: Re: PROD: p99 spike + 429s since 06:00PT — urgent

Cicero — thanks for the quick heads up and for the attachments. A few quick items before the call:
- We're spinning up a dedicated incident channel and an on-call handoff to SRE (cc: Rishi).
- Initial hypothesis: a sudden change in client retry behavior + our aggressive 429 throttles on the hosted API have created a retry amplification loop that increases queueing and token cache churn, driving p99 up.
- Immediate ask: can you temporarily disable aggressive client retries (back off to exponential jitter with max 2 retries) for affected routes while we triage? Even one-minute reduction in retries should reduce amplification.

I’m scheduling a 30-min war room now (15 minutes) and will share a join link. Sergio and Rishi — please bring the rate-limiter configs, recent kernel-selection changes, and any deployment rollouts between 04:00-07:00 PT.

Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0148

Subject: Re: PROD: p99 spike + 429s since 06:00PT — urgent

We're in the channel and seeing the same telemetry. Early notes from the serving plane:
- p99 spikes correlate with elevated retry counts from Brightlane's client identifiers (token prefixes BRT-*) and a sharp increase in short-lived connections.
- Our 429 enforcement policy (token bucket refill tuned aggressively to protect stability) is kicking in and returning 429 to bursts, which their client retries into, increasing effective concurrency.
- No new model deployments in the region between 04:00-07:00 PT, but there was a kernel-selection rollout pushed to a small subset of nodes that could alter per-token latency distribution.

Immediate mitigation proposal (15 min):
1) Temporarily relax 429 throttle thresholds for the Brightlane org by 30% (whitelist delta) for 20 minutes while we stabilize.
2) Apply a short-lived server-side retry-smoothing (add jitter and enforce per-conn serialization for same-client spikes).
3) Roll back the kernel-selection change on the small cohort if p99 does not improve after steps 1–2.

Marcus — can you prepare an ops playbook snippet to execute 1–2 and note risk/cost so we can tell Brightlane?

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Executing proposal 1 and 2 now:
- Pushed a temporary rate-limit delta for org Brightlane (org_id: BR-1009) +30% across hostedapi-us-east. Change id: RL-20270318-01. TTL: 20m.
- Enabled retry-smoothing gate on edge proxies for matching tokens (adds 30–50ms per-request but collapses retry bursts).
- Monitoring dashboards updated (link in channel).

Initial telemetry (08:56): p95 down ~20%, p99 down ~15%. 429 rate reduced by ~40% for affected clients. Still noisy; continuing to observe.

Marcus Lin

Follow-up from infra side after deeper trace sampling:
- Kernel-selection rollout to the cohort at 04:40 PT increased median token-execution time by ~8ms on those nodes; that amplified when retry bursts increased KV cache misses. Rolling that small cohort back (09:18 change id KS-20270318-rc1) returned median token times to baseline.
- The combination of kernel variance + rate-limit collisions created queueing across connection workers which increased tail latencies.

Next steps:
- We'll include a detailed change log and exact timestamps (RL-20270318-01, KS-20270318-rc1) in the postmortem and share safe client retry defaults.
- Laura, can you coordinate with Brightlane commercial contact on the credit/SLO conversation and produce a first estimate? Use the provisional impact window 06:00–09:30 PT and the telemetry slices attached.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Team — summary for execs and customer follow-up: 
- Incident window (provisional): 2027-03-18T06:00:00-07:00 to 2027-03-18T09:30:00-07:00. Root causes identified: (1) kernel-selection rollout increased token latency on a small cohort; (2) our 429 enforcement + Brightlane client aggressive retries produced a retry amplification loop, increasing queues and tail latency.
- Mitigations executed: RL-20270318-01 (temporary rate-limit delta +30% TTL 20m), retry-smoothing on edge, rollback KS-20270318-rc1. Observable effect: p95 ~25% reduction and p99 ~20% reduction from peak; 429s decreased ~40% for impacted clients.
- Impact: Brightlane reported ~10% of requests timed out at peak; commercial asks include an SLO-impact estimate and potential pro-rata credit.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Laura: draft customer-facing incident report and credit estimate (ETA: EOD today).
- Rishi/Infra: prepare technical postmortem with change logs and suggested kernel rollout gating (ETA: 72 hours).
- Sergio: propose server-side rate-limiter tuning defaults and a safer per-org emergency delta process (ETA: 48 hours).
- Marcus: add checklist step to temporarily reduce server-side throttles before major client-facing rollouts (ETA: next runbook update).

Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
